source_title: UNESCO Digital initiatives for Indigenous languages
unit_or_scope: global endangered and marginalized languages
direct_observation: 50 percent of spoken languages may be extinct or seriously endangered by 2100 and digital tools can support conservation revival and promotion
closed_stage: global risk digital intervention categories and community framing
missing_stage: everyday use transmission institutional access and control
next_test: follow a named language from tool creation to repeated use and child transmission

source_title: UNESCO 2025 Indigenous-language technology consultation
unit_or_scope: named language initiatives and language-resource gaps
direct_observation: missing documentation and online resources coexist with opportunities from AI OCR translation spell-checking and open archives
closed_stage: technology opportunity and infrastructure gap
missing_stage: dataset consent quality safety users ownership and outcomes
next_test: audit provenance dialect coverage correction and community governance

source_title: UNESCO Global Roadmap for Multilingualism in the Digital Era
unit_or_scope: all languages with focus on low-resource and endangered languages
direct_observation: roadmap calls for digital presence and language-community participation in decision-making data governance and tool development
closed_stage: policy architecture and participation requirement
missing_stage: product availability service completion quality and adoption
next_test: compare policy commitment with live tools and completed public-service encounters

source_title: UNESCO African languages blind spot of AI
unit_or_scope: African low-resource languages and AI systems
direct_observation: underrepresented languages show recognition and hallucination or translation failures while speech-data initiatives expand datasets
closed_stage: performance gap and dataset response
missing_stage: named user harm correction dialect trust access and outcome
next_test: test translated health legal and education interactions with speaker correction

source_title: WIPO documentation of traditional knowledge and traditional cultural expressions
unit_or_scope: Indigenous and local custodians and digital documentation
direct_observation: documentation can aid preservation but is not an end in itself and should be guided by risks benefits and holder control
closed_stage: IP data-governance boundary and consent risk
missing_stage: authority access restriction misuse benefit sharing and use
next_test: trace consent licensing withdrawal credit payment and community reuse

source_title: Welsh Government Welsh language technology and AI priorities
unit_or_scope: Wales and Cymraeg digital services and language technology
direct_observation: Welsh Government identifies priorities to increase daily use of Cymraeg, improve access to Welsh technology and improve AI and speech technologies through data sharing and related work
closed_stage: policy priorities and public commitment
missing_stage: live product availability service completion user quality daily use and speaker growth
next_test: match one funded or delivered tool to a named workplace school or public-service interaction and usage outcome

source_title: FirstVoices community language platform
unit_or_scope: Indigenous communities managing language sites and mobile or desktop access
direct_observation: FirstVoices states that Indigenous communities manage curate and share their languages and that community-uploaded data can be accessed through mobile and desktop apps
closed_stage: community-managed platform and access route
missing_stage: consent scope sensitive-data restrictions repeated use language learning transmission benefit sharing and long-term stewardship
next_test: select one FirstVoices language site and audit governance rules content activity learner use and community-controlled restrictions

source_title: University of Waikato Waikato-Maniapoto AI voice project
unit_or_scope: Waikato-Maniapoto te reo Maori dialect and named speaker voice project
direct_observation: University of Waikato reports an AI-generated Waikato-Maniapoto voice intended to help future generations hear and connect with their dialect and says the generated speech is difficult to distinguish from the original speaker
closed_stage: demonstrated dialect-specific voice technology and cultural-identity rationale
missing_stage: community authorization speaker rights daily use learner uptake pronunciation quality intergenerational transmission and misuse safeguards
next_test: trace project governance release conditions classroom or media deployment and evidence of repeated speaker or learner use

source_title: Welsh Government Annual Population Survey Welsh language data
unit_or_scope: Wales population aged three and over April 2024 to March 2025
direct_observation: APS estimated 828600 Welsh speakers and 423900 people reporting daily Welsh use; the release also reports 2021 Census 538300 speakers and warns that APS estimates are uncertain and should not be used as the official target measure
closed_stage: population and daily-use signal with measurement caveat
missing_stage: causal link to technology policy school or service intervention sustained cohort use and transmission
next_test: compare census National Survey and administrative or school data over time and link any changes to named intervention exposure

source_title: Estyn post-16 Welsh-language training evaluation
unit_or_scope: Welsh further education and apprenticeship practitioners and learning activities
direct_observation: Estyn reports increases in practitioners registered as able to work in Welsh and more learning activities with a small amount of Welsh-medium learning, but no direct data linking the change to training and no comparable increase in higher-intensity Welsh-medium or Welsh-only activity
closed_stage: staff-skill and low-intensity provision signal
missing_stage: student or apprentice repeated use higher-intensity provision teacher capacity causal attribution and long-term transmission
next_test: track named providers learner exposure language category progression and later Welsh-medium participation

source_title: Welsh Government technology and AI summary 2025 to 2026
unit_or_scope: Welsh language technology projects and public-sector use in Wales
direct_observation: Welsh Government reports nearly half a million new English-Welsh sentences, improved Welsh transcription and synthetic voices, Trawsgrifiwr and Macsen services, and examples of Welsh transcription used in government meetings and press work
closed_stage: data and tool production plus named workflow use
missing_stage: tool users usage volume accuracy correction repeat adoption service completion and impact on daily language use
next_test: obtain product telemetry or user records and compare workflow quality and repeat use across Welsh-speaking teams

source_title: Welsh Government technology summary and Mapio Cymru
unit_or_scope: Welsh-language geographic data and public maps
direct_observation: Welsh Government reports over 30000 Welsh names on OpenStreetMap, Welsh mapping services and community contribution; Senedd Cymru uses Mapio Cymru work as the basis for its constituency map
closed_stage: open geographic data and institutional map deployment
missing_stage: active users search or routing use place-name correction community participation and effect on Welsh-language place visibility
next_test: trace map usage analytics public-service reliance and whether users encounter or select Welsh place names

source_title: Business Wales Helo Blod milestone
unit_or_scope: Welsh businesses charities and community groups using free translation/advice
direct_observation: Business Wales reports Helo Blod translated one million words and reached more than 1000 businesses; a named business describes using translated social media product descriptions and Welsh labelling
closed_stage: service reach and named business implementation
missing_stage: repeat requests retained Welsh content customer interaction revenue or language-use change and representativeness of reported success
next_test: obtain current service records and a sample of participating businesses with pre/post Welsh-content and repeat-use measures

source_title: Welsh Government Annual Population Survey Welsh language data 2025 to 2026
unit_or_scope: Wales population aged three and over April 2025 to March 2026
direct_observation: APS estimated 843700 Welsh speakers and 446800 daily Welsh speakers; the release says the increase in speaker share is not statistically significant, APS accreditation is suspended, recent changes may reflect survey mode and the census remains the target measure
closed_stage: updated population and daily-use signal with explicit uncertainty
missing_stage: causal link to technology education or service interventions durable cohort use transmission and comparable census or National Survey trend
next_test: refresh against census and National Survey and link intervention exposure before interpreting movement as vitality

source_title: University of Waikato responsible Waikato-Maniapoto AI voice development
unit_or_scope: Waikato-Maniapoto dialect voice model and Māori language technology governance
direct_observation: University of Waikato reports that a local Māori language authority recorded thousands of sentences, Māori language experts supported development, Google funding was designated for protocols for responsible Māori language technologies and the voice remained in testing with release expected later
closed_stage: community participation and responsible-development intent plus pre-deployment readiness
missing_stage: release authority speaker rights data retention consent licensing misuse safeguards learner deployment repeated use pronunciation quality and transmission
next_test: locate release or deployment evidence and document the responsible-language protocol, access conditions and actual learner or media use

source_title: University of Waikato Summer Research project abstract for a new reo Māori AI voice
unit_or_scope: Waikato-Maniapoto synthetic voice research process and Te Hiku Media partnership
direct_observation: The project abstract specifies meetings with Te Hiku Media and an iwi speaker, approximately 30 hours of recordings, creation and testing of a new voice, documentation of the process and a final research poster as expected outputs
closed_stage: documented production workflow and partner route
missing_stage: actual recording consent terms speaker authority model release licensing quality results learner or media deployment and repeated use
next_test: locate the research poster or final report and confirm recording governance testing results and release conditions

source_title: TalkLink Annual Report 2024 Tua o te Pae
unit_or_scope: Te Hiku Media synthetic te reo Māori voice on Accent 1000 AAC device
direct_observation: TalkLink reports that Te Hiku Media demonstrated a te reo Māori male synthetic voice on an Accent 1000 communication device with acceptable quality and speed; the report describes a user receiving the voice on her own device and using it to deliver a mihi
closed_stage: device operation and named user communication proof of concept
missing_stage: number of users repeated use communication outcomes pronunciation evaluation broader device compatibility language and cultural participation outcomes
next_test: obtain phase-two user results and device deployment records with consent and outcome measures

source_title: TalkLink Annual Report 2025 Tua o te Pae
unit_or_scope: small Māori AAC-user test cohort and device compatibility
direct_observation: TalkLink reports Te Hiku Media voices being tested by a small number of Māori Accent-device users, positive feedback, preferred-gender voice options and ongoing work to adapt voices for Grid 3 and wider devices
closed_stage: small-cohort user testing and compatibility expansion
missing_stage: cohort size participant characteristics repeated daily use communication success language participation user safety and broad rollout
next_test: obtain test protocol participant counts feedback instrument and deployment status across Accent Tobii Dynavox and Grid 3

source_title: Te Taura Whiri i te Reo Māori and Google Maps text-to-speech
unit_or_scope: Māori place-name pronunciation in Google Maps
direct_observation: The Māori Language Commission reports a public Google Maps voice that pronounces Māori place names, a feedback route for errors, Commission-guided pronunciation, New Zealand Geographic Board data, Commission kaitiakitanga and Google licensing; the release is currently limited to Google Maps and does not cover dialect variation
closed_stage: public-facing geographic voice deployment with named stewardship and correction route
missing_stage: usage volume correction counts pronunciation quality by region or dialect long-term kaitiaki structure benefit sharing and effect on Māori-language use or place-name behavior
next_test: collect feedback or usage evidence and track whether the correction route changes model quality and whether the data-governance arrangement becomes durable

source_title: Welsh Government review of Welsh-language health and social-care data
unit_or_scope: Welsh language access and Active Offer measurement in health and social care
direct_observation: A 2026 review finds fragmented and inconsistently recorded data, coverage gaps, limited user-experience data and weak links between workforce skills and service delivery; it proposes 39 indicators across bilingual-service delivery demand workforce ability and future workforce ability
closed_stage: explicit outcome-measurement framework and evidence-gap diagnosis for language access in care
missing_stage: routine indicator production user-level service completion actual demand quality and safety organization-level comparability and whether technology changes access or experience
next_test: locate the indicator framework implementation owner and baseline data and test linkage between recorded Welsh skills service encounters and user experience

source_title: Sámi AI Lab Ábo Web Service
unit_or_scope: Sámi speech-to-text and translation for digital communication
direct_observation: The Sámi AI Lab reports a functional public-facing Ábo service that lets users speak naturally in Sámi and receive real-time transcription and translation, aimed at reducing language switching in digital spaces
closed_stage: public-facing speech-to-text or translation service and named Indigenous-led development route
missing_stage: active users language coverage transcription or translation error by dialect repeat use professional or educational outcomes privacy and community control of speech data
next_test: obtain service telemetry evaluation results language coverage and data-governance terms and test repeated use in professional or educational settings

source_title: Sámi AI Lab health cultural-generation and evaluation tracks
unit_or_scope: Sámi-specific clinical assessment cultural-generation tools and language or culture evaluation
direct_observation: Sámi AI Lab describes developmental work on Sámi-specific cognitive assessment culturally accurate generative tools for duodji and a Sámi understanding benchmark; it states that the benchmark and clinical platform remain in development and positions Sámi-led governance as a control surface
closed_stage: named high-stakes use cases evaluation agenda and Indigenous-led governance structure
missing_stage: validated clinical performance safety clinical adoption benchmark release cultural-fidelity testing data access rules traditional-knowledge restrictions and outcomes for Sámi users
next_test: locate benchmark artifacts clinical validation plans and data-access or community-governance documents before treating the work as deployed impact

source_title: Euskorpus Basque AI-language project
unit_or_scope: Basque corpus open models and sector-transfer ecosystem
direct_observation: The Basque Government reports a 10.55 million euro 2025 to 2027 public-private project led by Euskorpora to build a quality Basque corpus open-source base models and infrastructure identify applications across justice education health e-government and industry and transfer outputs to companies institutions and citizens; Spain’s ministry separately describes a three-year 5 million euro contribution to enrich public ALIA models and connect Basque resources to the European language-resource framework
closed_stage: funded language infrastructure public-private delivery coalition and explicit transfer pathway
missing_stage: corpus composition and rights model quality by dialect and task released artifacts sector deployments users service completion industrial uptake governance and whether infrastructure changes everyday Basque use
next_test: track phase completion released datasets and models sector pilots adoption and evidence that language technologies reach actual Basque users

source_title: Irish National Plan technical working group
unit_or_scope: Irish language technology governance across public-sector systems and AI
direct_observation: Ireland reports a cross-government technical group established under the 2024 to 2030 National Plan with representatives from central government social protection passports transport health policing local government revenue and public transport; its remit includes embedding Irish at the outset of AI and technology developments bilingual systems active offer reusable citizen language choice and employee support tools
closed_stage: upstream cross-government technical governance and named institutional ownership
missing_stage: meeting outputs standards adopted systems changed citizen language-choice reuse accessible services procurement compliance user experience and actual Irish-language service completion
next_test: review meeting minutes terms of reference and named system changes and trace a requirement from group decision to deployed service

source_title: Irish Action Plan for Irish Language Public Services 2026 to 2028
unit_or_scope: Irish language AI public-service design procurement and active offer
direct_observation: The Irish Government action plan calls for Irish-language elements in AI feasibility work on a single citizen language choice across common services proactive proofing tools and interfaces public feedback routes procurement compliance and technical working-group implementation
closed_stage: policy-to-procurement and service-design bridge for bilingual digital public services
missing_stage: funded delivery system-by-system implementation language-choice portability procurement enforcement feedback volume and resolution service use and quality in Irish
next_test: locate implementation owners budgets procurement clauses feedback records and completed Irish-language service encounters

source_title: AfriEval African-language data and evaluation platform
unit_or_scope: African-language data collection evaluation safety testing and provenance
direct_observation: AfriEval presents a workflow for collecting annotating evaluating and safety-testing speech text images documents and model outputs in languages including Swahili Yoruba Hausa Amharic Igbo and Zulu; it describes native-speaker and domain-expert review consent and licensing metadata multi-stage quality checks provenance benchmark traces and exportable datasets
closed_stage: named regional data and evaluation infrastructure with human and domain-expert controls
missing_stage: verified customer projects contributor compensation and consent practice language and dialect coverage benchmark results model improvements production deployment safety incidents and public benefit
next_test: locate public benchmark results project evidence and governance or compensation terms and connect platform activity to deployed African-language systems

source_title: East African Community AI sovereignty declaration
unit_or_scope: regional AI sovereignty language infrastructure and indigenous knowledge policy
direct_observation: The EAC reports that eight partner states resolved to establish a regional AI fund and promote systems speaking regional languages trained on East African data stored on regional infrastructure and governed by East Africans; it also names a regional centre of excellence AI alliance shared compute and data-centre infrastructure procurement reform and indigenous knowledge integration
closed_stage: regional geopolitical commitment linking language infrastructure financing governance and industrial policy
missing_stage: fund capitalization legal and data-governance instruments infrastructure delivery language models or services deployed cross-border adoption public outcomes inclusion of smaller languages and implementation accountability
next_test: track the declaration into fund decisions procurement contracts infrastructure milestones named models and deployments and country-level user outcomes
